gloss: to set off, to make stand out, to promote

definitions.gloss: to set off, to make stand out, to enhance
definitions.explanation: To make something look better or more prominent by contrast or complement. Often used for colors, flavors, and appearances.

definitions.gloss: to promote, to favor, to give a boost to
definitions.explanation: To help someone advance by giving them opportunities or support. Implies using one's influence or position to support another person.

examples.japanese: {黒|くろ}い{服|ふく}が{肌|はだ}の{白|しろ}さを{引|ひ}き{立|た}てる。
examples.english: The black clothing sets off the whiteness of the skin.

examples.japanese: ソースが{素材|そざい}の{味|あじ}を{引|ひ}き{立|た}てている。
examples.english: The sauce enhances the flavor of the ingredients.

examples.japanese: シンプルな{額縁|がくぶち}が{絵|え}の{美|うつく}しさをいっそう{引|ひ}き{立|た}てている。
examples.english: The simple frame makes the beauty of the painting stand out even more.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}に{引|ひ}き{立|た}てられて{出世|しゅっせ}した。
examples.english: I was promoted thanks to my boss's support.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{才能|さいのう}を{引|ひ}き{立|た}てるのが{私|わたし}の{役目|やくめ}だ。
examples.english: My role is to promote young talent.

examples.japanese: {先輩|せんぱい}に{引|ひ}き{立|た}てていただいたおかげで、{今|いま}の{自分|じぶん}がある。
examples.english: Thanks to the support my senior gave me, I am where I am today.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound verb combining {引|ひ}く (to pull) and {立|た}てる (to make stand). The overall meaning centers on making something stand out or come forward.

GRAMMAR:
Ichidan verb. Transitive — takes を for the thing being enhanced or the person being promoted.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {味|あじ}を{引|ひ}き{立|た}てる: to bring out the flavor
- {美|うつく}しさを{引|ひ}き{立|た}てる: to enhance the beauty
- {才能|さいのう}を{引|ひ}き{立|た}てる: to promote talent
- {互|たが}いに{引|ひ}き{立|た}て{合|あ}う: to set each other off, to complement each other
